summary: Bug fix testing for keyboard input blocking in SCORM exports. Both bug fixes verified: (1) player.js keyboard navigation now skips when e.target is input/textarea/contentEditable (line 1684-1689), (2) tutor.js input calls e.stopPropagation() on keydown/keyup/keypress events (lines 79-89). All 9 tests passed including health endpoint, tutor settings API, tutor chat API, SCORM export validation, and source file verification.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Keyboard input bug fix in SCORM exports has been verified. The fix ensures that when users type in the AI Tutor chat input (or any input/textarea), the SCORM player's keyboard navigation (ArrowLeft/Right, Space, Enter, Backspace, f/F) does not intercept the events. Two-layer protection: (1) player.js checks e.target tagName before handling shortcuts, (2) tutor.js calls stopPropagation on all keyboard events. Future SCORM exports will include these fixes. Existing already-exported packages are NOT affected - users must re-export.

bug_fix_verification.issue: AI Tutor widget in SCORM exports was blocking keyboard input - SCORM player's keyboard navigation intercepted events
bug_fix_verification.root_cause: player.js keyboard handler processed all keydown events without checking if target was an input element
bug_fix_verification.fix_details_1: Added check: if (tag === 'input' || tag === 'textarea' || e.target.isContentEditable) return;
bug_fix_verification.fix_details_2: Added e.stopPropagation() to keydown, keyup, and keypress event listeners on tutor input
